purpose: Preserve the substantive R1 findings that were identified in the research discussion but were not fully captured as a single durable artifact before the Thunder deletion after backup completeness was incorrectly confirmed.

scope.interpretation: R1 is a market-wide bear-to-bull recovery process. Evidence can accumulate in different order and timing; this is morphology/evidence, not a rigid fixed-day gate.

findings.name: Extreme prior destruction establishes the recovery context
findings.finding: R1 begins from substantial prior market damage. The destruction context matters because an ordinary pullback bounce is not the same phenomenon as emergence from a major bear/crash state.

findings.name: Initial price stabilization or impulse is early evidence but is not sufficient
findings.finding: True recoveries commonly begin with a strong price stabilization/impulse, but adversarial GFC false rallies demonstrated that a large bounce by itself cannot identify durable recovery.
findings.role: early evidence; explicitly falsified as standalone rule

findings.name: Breadth conversion has level, velocity/acceleration, and timing information
findings.finding: The strongest true-recovery discriminator was not merely higher breadth but a market-wide conversion that can arrive late and explosively. Breadth level and breadth velocity/acceleration are distinct evidence. In 2009 breadth-positive-20 rose from about 14.8% at day 5 to 53.9% at day 7 and 82.0% at day 10; by day 15 it was 91.8%. In 2020 breadth remained extremely weak through day 7 (~1.0%) before converting later, reaching the broad-recovery region by day 15. A fixed requirement that breadth must lead price would therefore reject a genuine V-shaped recovery.

findings.name: Breadth must persist rather than merely spike
findings.finding: A one- or two-session breadth surge is not equivalent to recovery. Genuine recoveries showed broader cross-sectional persistence; false rallies could temporarily improve breadth and then stall or roll over. Breadth persistence is therefore separate from breadth level and acceleration.

findings.name: Failed rebounds must continue to disappear
findings.finding: As true recovery develops, the fraction of attempted rebounds that fail falls materially and continues falling. In the GFC true-recovery path fail20 fell from 0.75 at day 5 to 0.50 at day 10 and 0.30 at day 15. The November 2008 false rally instead deteriorated from 0.55 at day 5 to 0.65 at day 10. The day5-to-day10 divergence was -0.25 for the March true recovery versus +0.10 for the November false rally.

findings.name: Short-trend repair confirms that the bounce is becoming structural
findings.finding: True recovery increasingly repairs short and then medium trend structure rather than remaining a countertrend bounce. In the GFC day5-to-day10 true-recovery transition, gap20 improved by about +0.0707, gap50 by +0.0919, slope20 by +0.0291 and slope50 by +0.0144. The November false-rally transition showed almost no comparable structural repair.

findings.name: Stress normalization and recovery retention complete the morphology but may lag
findings.finding: VIX/VVIX and funding/credit stress generally normalize as recovery becomes durable, while price retains enough of the recovery through pullbacks. Stress improvement need not precede the price/breadth turn and can lag substantially, so it should add evidence rather than serve as an early mandatory gate.

cross_episode_rule.finding: The recurring morphology is destruction -> price stabilization/impulse -> breadth conversion -> failed-rebound improvement -> trend repair -> broader persistence -> stress normalization, but the sequence is descriptive rather than a mandatory ordering.
cross_episode_rule.timing: Order and timing vary materially by episode. For example, 2009 reached +10% by about day 3, breadth >80% by day 10 and EMA50 repair around day 7; 2020 reached +10% on day 1 but breadth >80% only around day 15 and EMA50 repair around day 30.
cross_episode_rule.governance: Do not hard-code a fixed number of sessions after the trough, require breadth to lead price, or require all dimensions to cross simultaneously.

gfc_adversarial_control.conclusion: The true recovery separated most strongly through continuing cross-sectional conversion, declining failed rebounds, and trend repair—not through price bounce magnitude alone.

relationship_to_running_ga.rule: This artifact preserves and clarifies R1 research. It does not retroactively alter the already-running four-fold DEV117 GA. Any later use beyond the dimensions already frozen must be a separately versioned post-run decision.
